reference: Hand-built package readiness states in the tool-neutral input vocabulary of SPEC-packagereadiness.md section 13.1 (revision 2026-09-22.1, read 2026-09-22): the five presets of section 9 with every expectation stated under them, each of the 39 gate criteria of section 5.2 with at least one state that makes it fail or except and one that makes it pass, each of the 17 data findings of section 5.3 with a triggering and a non-triggering state, the review-code table of section 3.5 (codes 1, 2, 3, 4, empty, invalid and the absent container), the derived predicates of section 3.4 (current requisition, governing bid evaluation, dispositioned, affects(G), closed, FAT-origin, package and system matching, dossiers of a package, order maturity and open holds), the combination and precedence rules of sections 4.2 and 4.6, the flag rule of section 4.5 over met, exception, not_met, no_data and na, the n/a order of section 4.4, the frontier of section 4.7, the counts of section 4.8, project criteria of both kinds (section 3.8), the written readiness rows and the derived-id collision of section 7.3, and the package load mapping of section 7.1 with its ignored sections. Every reference value is stated by hand in the case builders of packagereadiness-ref.py and independently recomputed by the standard-library engine in the same file, which re-implements sections 3 to 6 without access to the tool code; the builder aborts if the two disagree, so no value in this file is a transcript of one of them alone.
reference_citations: tools.petrov.re SPEC-packagereadiness.md revision 2026-09-22.1 (_docs/SPEC-packagereadiness.md) - Conventions (norm, empty, id comparison), 3 (data model, review codes, flags, n/a, project criteria, id rules), 4 (criterion results, combination, dependencies, n/a, flags, verdict, frontier, counts), 5.2 (the 39 gate criteria), 5.3 (the 17 data findings), 6 (verdict logic and the blocker / exception / gap / observation lists), 7.1 and 7.3 (package load and written register), 9 (the five presets and their expected results), 13 (corpus interface), 15 (acceptance criteria). Read 2026-09-22.

IEC 62381:2024 Ed. 3.0, 'Automation systems in the process industry - Factory acceptance test (FAT), site acceptance test (SAT) and site integration test (SIT)' - cited by the spec (5.1) for 3.1.8 FAT, 3.1.16 punch list, 5.3.3 documentation before FAT, 5.3.4 test plan, 5.4 FAT punch list, 5.5.2 FAT report and 5.6 FAT completion, which are the basis of PAC-R-201, PAC-R-203, PAC-R-301 and PAC-R-302. This corpus does not re-derive the standard: it grades the spec's rules, and the citation records where their engineering basis comes from.

NORSOK Z-CR-007 Rev. 1 (1996), 'Mechanical completion and commissioning' - cited by the spec (5.1) for status PA / category A work that must be completed before the milestone and category B work that may be carried, which is why PAC-R-302 is a blocker and PAC-R-303 is major at delivery. The spec's own open question Q5 records that PAC-R-503 (category B at turnover) is stricter than Annex A; the corpus follows the spec.

ISO 9001:2015 section 8.6 'Release of products and services' - cited by the spec (5.1) as the basis for treating the delivery gate as a release decision (PAC-R-305, PAC-R-306). The spec notes this edition was withdrawn in September 2026 and that ISO 9001:2026 clause numbering was not verified; the corpus therefore grades no clause of either edition.

tolerance: Exact categorical equality, sets compared without order, as SPEC-packagereadiness.md 13.2 states. Every graded output is a word from a closed vocabulary (verdict, criterion result, raw result, na source, next gate, headline, save refused, finding present) or an integer count of criteria; there is no physical quantity and no floating-point arithmetic anywhere in the tool (spec 3 and 4: 'no arithmetic beyond counts'), so no numeric tolerance exists to choose. The counts are derived by counting the criteria of a gate, which is why they are stated as exact integers: for gate po that is 12 built-in criteria plus the project criteria of the case, 5 for fat, 7 for delivery, 6 for installation and 9 for turnover. Blocker, exception, gap and observation lists are compared as sets of 'criterion|target_kind|target_id' strings, with an empty field where the spec produces a null target id or an untyped reference; gap and observation lists hold criterion ids only. tol is 'exact' on every check.

not_benchmarked: Whether the built-in gate criteria are the right criteria for a real project (spec limitation 2 and section 14): the corpus grades the rules as specified, not their adequacy.
Whether an upstream register row is technically correct - that a code-1 document is a good document, that an accepted dossier should have been accepted (spec limitation 3).
Reason strings, criterion titles, basis strings and the wording of findings: only the rule id, the result, the severity-driven list membership and the target kind and id are graded, as 13.2 allows.
The UI and the report: panels, the readiness matrix figure, the mobile layout, the PDF, the seven languages, the permalink and the record shape (spec 10, 11, 13.2 item 8 partially).
The Python export: the spec declines it (section 12), so there is nothing to reproduce; the corpus asserts no script behaviour.

Storage and boot behaviour: peek, the Load banner, a throwing localStorage, the conflict choice and the byte-identical merge of other packages' rows on save (spec 7.2, 7.3, 13.2 item 8). The load mapping itself is graded through two package cases; the save is graded only as the row ids, verdicts, is_next flags and the refusal on a derived-id collision.
ISO 9001:2026 clause numbering, which spec 5.1 states was not verified.
